You hear part of a conversation between a junior and senior doctor on how to
 interpret the results of an investigation.
 What does the senior doctor clarify about the results of the investigation?
A. That the results clearly point to portal hypertension
B. That the results are not sufficient to come to a definite diagnosis
 yet
C. That the medical history allows them to rule out cirrhosis

 The speaker points out that this approach is better than…
A. One not focused specifically on this behavior
B. One used by other types of specialties
C. One focused on patient´s worries and desires

 What does the doctor explain to the patient?
A. When they can insert the implant
B. How they will insert the implant
C. Why they will insert the implant

 medication.
 What does the nurse point out about the patient’s medication?

B. He depends on his wife to get painkillers from the doctors in the
 hospital.
C. He is mixing over-the-counter and prescribed medications.

 The doctor referring the patient explains that…
A. The previous diagnosis was made by a doctor at another practice.
B. The previous diagnosis was made by a specialist in another field.

 working.

A. Because of all of the benefits it is known to have

A. Include a larger number of total subjects

A. Who have any type of severe illness
B. Who are having serious problems with sputum

A. Getting a large specimen from the patient

A. Recover quickly after the procedure is over
B. Produce a quality sample of sputum
C. Feel comfortable with the procedure

Dr Coffey suggests changing the procedure when…
A. A patient is physically not able to cough
B. A patient is taking certain medication
C. A patient does not want to give consent
